calls.head: The Flyers feed on mistakes, and the Hurricanes make them
calls.body: The Hurricanes give up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most, and the Flyers pounce.
calls.call: The Flyers get at least their usual 7.9% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Philadelphia 2nd for chances off turnovers (7.9% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Carolina 25th for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: 0.0% of Philadelphia’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.9%.

calls.head: Expect the Hurricanes to fire from everywhere
calls.body: The Hurricanes shoot a lot, and the Flyers are near the bottom of the league at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.
calls.call: The Hurricanes take at least their usual 61.0 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Carolina 6th for shot volume (61.0 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Philadelphia 27th for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Carolina took 80.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 61.0.

calls.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
calls.body: The Hurricanes and the Flyers are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 119.
calls.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): Carolina 128 (2nd), Philadelphia 110 (7th)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 98, against their usual 119 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).

PHI.head: We had this close to even (46% for Philadelphia), and it went Carolina’s way.

CAR.head: We had this close to even (54% for Carolina), and Carolina came through.

surprises.head: Carolina hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Carolina’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 60, against their usual 128 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 125 games.
surprises.flipped: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams

surprises.head: Philadelphia tried a different line
surprises.body: C. Grundstrom, O. Tippett, T. Zegras played 11:36 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Philadelphia’s usual lines.

story.head: Gostisbehere wins it in overtime
paras: Sebastian Aho scored twice, opening the scoring 10 seconds in. The game was tied twice. Shayne Gostisbehere won it 2:51 into overtime.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Hurricanes win about four in five. The Flyers tried a line they hadn’t used before: Carl Grundstrom, Owen Tippett and Trevor Zegras.
